scope: Targeted primary literature on observed large flakes, aggregate scaling, evolving geometry and hydrodynamic collision efficiency; companion to strength_literature.md. No systematic review or full scholarly admission claimed.
external_bytes: No external source bytes stored in the repository. Sources read through web text extraction and publisher-indexed results; no raw-source hash claimed.

sources.authors: R. Paul Lawson, Ronald E. Stewart, J. Walter Strapp and George A. Isaac
sources.title: Aircraft observations of the origin and growth of very large snowflakes
sources.reading_extent: Author-uploaded paper text: abstract, instrumentation, observations, surface collection and summary; figure captions. No image digitization.
sources.evidence: Direct airborne imaging and ground collection of centimetre aggregates.
sources.limit: Approximately 5 cm airborne imaging range; no physical maximum established.
sources.retrieval_failure: Direct Wiley full-text open failed; author-uploaded primary paper text obtained.

sources.authors: R. Paul Lawson, Ronald E. Stewart and Leigh J. Angus
sources.title: Observations and Numerical Simulations of the Origin and Development of Very Large Snowflakes
sources.reading_extent: Publisher-indexed full text: abstract, introduction, observations/model synthesis, section 4c, conclusions and relevant captions.
sources.evidence: Observed large-flake storm interpreted with mesoscale and microphysical models.
sources.limit: Warm-layer breakup suppression is an inferred case mechanism, not a direct contact-strength measurement.
sources.retrieval_failure: Direct page open returned 403 after publisher-indexed text was retrieved.

sources.authors: C. D. Westbrook, R. C. Ball, P. R. Field and A. J. Heymsfield
sources.title: Universality in snowflake aggregation
sources.reading_extent: Publisher text: model assumptions, fractal exponent, distribution scaling, observational comparisons and captions.
sources.evidence: Rigid geometric aggregation compared with cirrus observations.
sources.limit: No fracture, mechanical bond calculation or lunar validation.

sources.authors: C. D. Westbrook, R. C. Ball, P. R. Field and A. J. Heymsfield
sources.title: Theory of growth by differential sedimentation, with application to snowflake formation
sources.reading_extent: Sections II–IV and opening V; equations 1–14; PDF text and figure captions. Publisher abstract verified identity; no full-paper rendering review.
sources.evidence: Scaling argument and geometric simulation for structural feedback in differential sedimentation.
sources.limit: Dilute binary encounters, permanent rigid contacts, no hydrodynamic deflection. Local 1.9-law asymptotics in the note are our derivation, not paper results.

sources.authors: T. H. M. Stein, C. D. Westbrook and J. C. Nicol
sources.title: Fractal geometry of aggregate snowflakes revealed by triple-wavelength radar measurements
sources.reading_extent: Abstract, sections 1–3, geometry/size integration assumptions and experimental setup.
sources.evidence: Remote retrieval supports fractal dimensions near two.
sources.limit: Size integration truncated at 20 mm; no decimetre strength inference.

sources.authors: Axel Seifert, Fabian Jakub, Christoph Siewert, Leonie von Terzi and Stefan Kneifel
sources.title: On the Geometry of Aggregate Snowflakes
sources.reading_extent: Preprint sections 2–3 and stochastic representation context; published indexed metadata and geometry results. Published coefficient tables not compared exhaustively with v1.
sources.evidence: Synthetic joint geometry from 2–2048 monomers and mean monomer size 50–500 micrometres.
sources.limit: Contact regularization is geometric, not mechanical; present runs retain v1 provenance.
sources.retrieval_failure: Direct Tellus page opens failed; Reference Global full page timed out. Publisher-indexed content and arXiv v1 were accessible.

sources.authors: C. D. Westbrook, R. J. Hogan and A. J. Illingworth
sources.title: The Capacitance of Pristine Ice Crystals and Aggregate Snowflakes
sources.reading_extent: Abstract, section 3e, Figures 12–14 captions, screening discussion and opening discussion; published identity checked.
sources.evidence: Diffusive capacitance computed for about 1000 synthetic aggregates, compared with previously reported sublimation retrieval.
sources.limit: Capacitance is distinct from aerodynamic collision efficiency, optical cross section and strength.

sources.authors: Axel Seifert, Jussi Leinonen, Christoph Siewert and Stefan Kneifel
sources.title: The Geometry of Rimed Aggregate Snowflakes: A Modeling Study
sources.publication: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems 11, 712–731 (2019)
sources.reading_extent: Publisher-indexed sections 2, geometric transition discussion, 3.5, idealized column setup and conclusions.
sources.evidence: Explicit geometric aggregation/riming with prescribed rime compaction.
sources.limit: Mean 200 micrometre monomers, 40 micrometre droplets; no branch-strength validation at decimetre scale.

sources.title: McSnow: A Monte-Carlo Particle Model for Riming and Aggregation of Ice Particles in a Multidimensional Microphysical Phase Space
sources.publication: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems 10, 187–206 (2018)
sources.reading_extent: Abstract and sections 2.2.2–2.2.5, 2.4, and Figure 3 collision-efficiency discussion.
sources.evidence: Implementation precedent separating hydrodynamic interception, sticking and riming state.
sources.limit: Describes a parameterization and numerical controls; paper does not claim observational validation of its full model.

sources.authors: Jan-Niklas Welss, Christoph Siewert and Axel Seifert
sources.title: Explicit Habit-Prediction in the Lagrangian Super-Particle Ice Microphysics Model McSnow
sources.publication: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems 16, e2023MS003805 (2024)
sources.reading_extent: Abstract, introduction, section 2.2 collision-efficiency discussion, section 3.2 atmospheric dependence, ventilation discussion and conclusions excerpts.
sources.evidence: Habit-dependent aerodynamic parameterization, comparisons with laboratory particle analogues and cloud observations.
sources.limit: No direct lunar-gravity or giant-aggregate validation; Böhm framework explicitly treated as parameterization.
